title: Multiverses and the equation
changes: The multiverse: from universe 5 on, you can enter a new multiverse. Your universes and dark matter start over, and your dark matter turns into strings. Each string makes you produce 25% more, forever, and strings buy 12 multiverse upgrades, such as starting in universe 2 or keeping your dark matter upgrades.

The equation, a new tab in the top bar: spend your detector clicks on the terms of the equation of everything, from the Standard Model to string theory. Every symbol gives +0.5% data and funding, and your equation stays with you in every universe and multiverse.

7 new research topics, each with its own info page: antimatter gravity, magnetic monopoles, muon g−2 and glueballs in universes 2 to 5, and supersymmetry, extra dimensions and string theory in multiverses 2 to 4.
6 new kinds of staff: Engineers, Data Scientists and Theorists in universes 3, 4 and 6, and Parallel Selves, Boltzmann Brains and Universe Builders in multiverses 2 to 4.
42 new upgrades for the new research and staff, for universes 7 to 17 and for multiverses 2 to 6.
79 new achievements for the new research and staff, multiverses, strings and the equation.
Dark matter now counts the data collected in the current multiverse. Achievements for universes and dark matter still count every multiverse.
Very big numbers use R and Q after Y, and scientific notation after that.
Quick level-ups share one pop-up instead of piling up.

title: Dark matter from data
changes: Dark matter now comes from the data you collect: the first at 1T data, 10 at 1P and 100 at 1E, counting every universe. The Particle Expansion window shows how close you are.
14 new HR upgrades: a sixth upgrade for each of the original staff once you have 100, a fifth for the newer staff once you have 50, and three team upgrades: Open Office, Lab Retreat and Espresso Bar.
Particle skins have moved to the top bar.
8 more secret achievements, for 18 in all.

title: Particle skins
changes: Particle skins: 12 looks for the event display, from Neon and Bubble Chamber to Plasma and Cosmic. They unlock as you earn achievements. Find them in the new Skins tab of the Achievements window, or with the brush button on the detector.
24 new upgrades: one for each of the original research topics, a fifth upgrade for each of the original staff once you have 50, and upgrades that unlock at levels 10, 30 and 50.
33 new achievements for upgrades bought, staff hired, research levels and boosts over all your universes, bigger milestones, and 2 more secrets.
The level bar and boosts now look like the rest of the game, and level-ups show a pop-up like achievements.
Levels come at a steadier pace, so the higher ones can actually be reached.
Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on a Mac) saves the game.

title: Levels, Particle Expansion and dark mode
changes: Levels: earn XP from clicking, research, hiring, upgrades, anomalies and achievements. The level bar sits under the detector, and every level-up lets you choose one of three boosts.
Particle Expansion: reset your lab to turn reputation into dark matter. Each dark matter makes you produce 10% more, forever, and buys 12 dark matter upgrades such as an automatic trigger.
9 new upgrades that only appear after you have expanded the universe.

New effects in the event display as you upgrade your colliders and make discoveries: photons, jets, golden Higgs events, pile-up, displaced vertices, missing energy, annihilations, heavy-ion collisions and more. The detector's info page lists them all.
21 new achievements for levels, expansions and dark matter, including 8 secret ones. Can you find them?
Settings, with a dark mode, scientific number format, detector effect quality and options to hide pop-ups or reduce motion.
On short windows the detector now shrinks so the counters stay in view.
Fixed the price of an upgrade showing as a gain, and the event display speeding up after resizing the window.

title: 100 new things
changes: 3 new kinds of staff: Citizen Scientists, Collaboration Spokespersons and Directors-General.
5 new research topics, each with its own info page: neutrino oscillations, quark–gluon plasma, antihydrogen, tetraquarks and pentaquarks.
32 new upgrades, including the first ones that raise your funding, upgrades for anomalies and time away, and two new colliders.
60 new achievements for the new staff and research, reputation, data per click, anomalies, time played and bigger totals.
The new staff and research start where the original ones run out, so there is always something to work towards.
Fixed missing icons on the LHCb upgrade and the data processed achievements.

title: Anomalies
changes: Rare anomalies now appear on the detector every few minutes. Click one before it fades for a data burst, a funding windfall or a 30 second data boost.
Three new achievements for catching anomalies.
Research can now be done ×1, ×10 or as many levels as you can afford at once.
This update log, so you can see what has changed.

title: Quality of life
changes: Your lab keeps earning while the game is closed, for up to 24 hours.
Data and funding per second are shown under the counters.
The Statistics window shows time played, rates, staff, research levels and achievements.
Hire staff ×1, ×10 or as many as you can afford at once.
Export your save as a code and import it again, for backups or to move to another device.

title: The Particle Simulation
changes: The game is now called The Particle Simulation.
